claims: Mount Sinai (Jebel Musa) is located in Egypt's Sinai Peninsula.
Mount Sinai (Jebel Musa) is 7,497 feet (2,285 meters) high.
Mount Sinai is revered by Judaism, Christianity, and Islam as the biblical site where Moses received the Ten Commandments.
St. Catherine's Monastery is at the base of Mount Sinai.
Mount Sinai is traditionally identified as the place where God spoke to Moses and revealed the Law.
St. Catherine's Monastery is the site of the Burning Bush, where Moses is believed to have first spoken with God.
Mount Sinai is known as Jebel Musa (Mountain of Moses) or Mount Horeb.
Mount Sinai is situated in the south-central part of the Sinai Peninsula in Egypt.
The peak of Mount Sinai stands at roughly 2,285 meters (7,497 feet) above sea level.
Jebel Musa is the traditional site of Mount Sinai.
Some scholars have proposed alternative locations for Mount Sinai in the northern Negev Desert, Jordan, or Saudi Arabia.
There are two main paths to the summit of Mount Sinai.
Siket El Bashait is the longer, shallower route to the summit of Mount Sinai that takes about 2.5 hours on foot.
Camels can be used for part of the way on Siket El Bashait.
Siket Sayidna Musa is a steeper, more direct path to the summit of Mount Sinai consisting of 3,750 "steps of penitence" located in the ravine behind the monastery.
St. Catherine's Monastery is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
St. Catherine's Monastery was built in the 6th century.
St. Catherine's Monastery is the oldest continuously inhabited Christian monastery.
Archaeological studies at the site have found evidence of early human activity, including stone structures and ancient tools.
Countless ancient artifacts have been found in the library of St. Catherine's Monastery.
